title: Router queue prioritization imbalance causing small-request starvation and TTFT regression
creator: Amelia Park
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sudden increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) for short chat priming requests and an overall drop in tokens/sec throughput. Impacted tenants include small-burst interactive apps and PLG evaluation tests. Root cause analysis indicates a recent scheduler heuristic change that unintentionally deprioritized short, low-token requests and caused increased KV cache churn for priming tokens, producing higher first-token latency and reduced aggregate token throughput.
comments: 2026-03-01 | Amelia Park: Ticket created after customer escalation from AcmeAI and internal Canary alerts. Initial triage shows TTFT up 3x on requests < 16 tokens in hosted region us-west-2. Linked to increase in cache misses and longer batch fill times.

2026-03-02 | Diego Hernandez: Confirmed regression introduced by scheduler change 'fairness-v2' merged on 2026-02-27 (commit 7f3c9a). Heuristic now applies a size-penalty weight that heavily favors large requests in multiplex queues. Observed starvation of small requests and eviction of warmed KV entries used for priming.

2026-03-03 | Priya Nair (SRE): Emergency mitigation applied: temporarily revert size-penalty in router config for hosted pools and lower multiplex batch target from 64 to 32, which recovered TTFT by ~45% in canary. Not safe to roll to all pools without deeper fixes.

2026-03-04 | Diego Hernandez: Load test runs show tokens/sec drop of ~20% when heuristics favor large requests under heterogeneous workload. Identified two compounding factors: (1) aggressive prefetch eviction logic that assumes long-lived hot keys, (2) lack of a small-request fast-lane in the scheduler.

2026-03-06 | Maya Chen (Runtime lead): Drafted a two-phase plan: immediate config rollback + adaptive throttling for large multi-context batches; medium-term: scheduler redesign to include explicit lanes and KV pinning for priming sequences.

2026-03-08 | Diego Hernandez: Created experimental branch scheduler/small-fastlane with unit/integration tests. Ran synthetic traffic that mixes 90% short priming calls with 10% long generation calls; small-lane recovers TTFT to baseline and restores tokens/sec within 95% of original.
2026-03-10 | Customer Success: AcmeAI verified improved latency on a staging snapshot after canary change. They asked for a faster timeline for Dedicated pools due to SLA impact.

2026-03-12 | Diego Hernandez: Open PR ready for review (see related_prs). Planning canary rollout to hosted, then Dedicated, then a guidance doc for Private customers. Post-release tests scheduled in perf cluster C.
2026-03-13 | Maya Chen: Added rollout checklist and required monitoring dashboards. Marked follow-ups for postmortem and scheduler test hardening.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a multiplex worker configured with fairness-v2 enabled
2) Generate mixed workload: 90% requests with prompt length <16 tokens (priming), 10% long generation requests (>=512 tokens)
3) Measure TTFT distribution and tokens/sec over 30 minutes; observe elevated p95 TTFT and reduced aggregate tokens/sec compared to pre-change baseline
4) Capture KV cache hit rate for priming keys and scheduler queue occupancy by request size
mitigation: Applied immediate rollback of size-penalty config in hosted canary pools and reduced multiplex target batch size to 32. This temporary change reduced TTFT for small requests by ~45% and restored tokens/sec partially. Communicated to Dedicated owners to pause fairness-v2 rollout until fix merges. For Private customers, provided rollback instructions and a checklist.
proposed_fix: 1) Implement 'small-request fast lane' in scheduler that guarantees a bounded service window for requests under a token threshold and pins their KV priming keys to avoid eviction; 2) Modify fairness scoring to include recent KV priming hit-rate as a positive signal; 3) Add unit and perf tests simulating heterogeneous workloads; 4) Backfill canary and chaos testing in perf clusters.
rollout_plan: Phase A (Canary): deploy scheduler small-lane to 2 canary hosts in staging and hosted-canary cluster (48h validation). Phase B (Gradual): 10% hosted -> 50% -> 100% over 72h with metric gates (p95 TTFT, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization). Phase C (Dedicated): apply to selected reserved pools after host-level validation. Phase D (Private): publish patch and detailed upgrade guide; offer assisted upgrade to enterprise customers.
test_plan: Synthetic mixed-workload perf harness (90/10 short/long) across model family (gpt-like 1.3B, 7B, and 70B) with sequence lengths from 8 to 2048. Automated p95/p99 TTFT regression thresholds, tokens/sec stability checks, KV priming hit-rate assertions. Run end-to-end smoke and canary monitors before and after each rollout step.
